verses.text: Now when the day of Pentecost had come, they were all with one accord in one place.
Suddenly there came from the sky a sound like the rushing of a mighty wind, and it filled all the house where they were sitting.
Tongues like fire appeared and were distributed to them, and one sat on each of them.
They were all filled with the Holy Spirit, and began to speak with other languages, as the Spirit gave them the ability to speak.
Now there were dwelling in Jerusalem Jews, devout men, from every nation under the sky.
When this sound was heard, the multitude came together, and were bewildered, because everyone heard them speaking in his own language.
They were all amazed and marveled, saying to one another, “Behold, aren’t all these who speak Galileans?
How do we hear, everyone in our own native language?
Parthians, Medes, Elamites, and people from Mesopotamia, Judea, Cappadocia, Pontus, Asia,
Phrygia, Pamphylia, Egypt, the parts of Libya around Cyrene, visitors from Rome, both Jews and proselytes,
Cretans and Arabians: we hear them speaking in our languages the mighty works of God!”
They were all amazed, and were perplexed, saying to one another, “What does this mean?”
Others, mocking, said, “They are filled with new wine.”
But Peter, standing up with the eleven, lifted up his voice, and spoke out to them, “You men of Judea, and all you who dwell at Jerusalem, let this be known to you, and listen to my words.
For these aren’t drunken, as you suppose, seeing it is only the third hour of the day.
But this is what has been spoken through the prophet Joel:
‘It will be in the last days, says God, that I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh. Your sons and your daughters will prophesy. Your young men will see visions. Your old men will dream dreams.
Yes, and on my servants and on my handmaidens in those days, I will pour out my Spirit, and they will prophesy.
I will show wonders in the sky above, and signs on the earth beneath; blood, and fire, and billows of smoke.
The sun will be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before the great and glorious day of the Lord comes.
It will be that whoever will call on the name of the Lord will be saved.’
“Men of Israel, hear these words! Jesus of Nazareth, a man approved by God to you by mighty works and wonders and signs which God did by him among you, even as you yourselves know,
him, being delivered up by the determined counsel and foreknowledge of God, you have taken by the hand of lawless men, crucified and killed;
whom God raised up, having freed him from the agony of death, because it was not possible that he should be held by it.
For David says concerning him, ‘I saw the Lord always before my face, For he is on my right hand, that I should not be moved.
Therefore my heart was glad, and my tongue rejoiced. Moreover my flesh also will dwell in hope;
because you will not leave my soul in Hades,  neither will you allow your Holy One to see decay.
You made known to me the ways of life. You will make me full of gladness with your presence.’
“Brothers, I may tell you freely of the patriarch David, that he both died and was buried, and his tomb is with us to this day.
Therefore, being a prophet, and knowing that God had sworn with an oath to him that of the fruit of his body, according to the flesh, he would raise up the Christ to sit on his throne,
he foreseeing this spoke about the resurrection of the Christ, that neither was his soul left in Hades,  nor did his flesh see decay.
This Jesus God raised up, to which we all are witnesses.
Being therefore exalted by the right hand of God, and having received from the Father the promise of the Holy Spirit, he has poured out this, which you now see and hear.
For David didn’t ascend into the heavens, but he says himself, ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit by my right hand,
until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet.”’
“Let all the house of Israel therefore know certainly that God has made him both Lord and Christ, this Jesus whom you crucified.”
Now when they heard this, they were cut to the heart, and said to Peter and the rest of the apostles, “Brothers, what shall we do?”
Peter said to them, “Repent, and be baptized, every one of you, in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of sins, and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.
For the promise is to you, and to your children, and to all who are far off, even as many as the Lord our God will call to himself.”
With many other words he testified, and exhorted them, saying, “Save yourselves from this crooked generation!”
Then those who gladly received his word were baptized. There were added that day about three thousand souls.
They continued steadfastly in the apostles’ teaching and fellowship, in the breaking of bread, and prayer.
Fear came on every soul, and many wonders and signs were done through the apostles.
All who believed were together, and had all things in common.
They sold their possessions and goods, and distributed them to all, according as anyone had need.
Day by day, continuing steadfastly with one accord in the temple, and breaking bread at home, they took their food with gladness and singleness of heart,
praising God, and having favor with all the people. The Lord added to the assembly day by day those who were being saved.

footnotes.content: Pentecost—fifty days after Passover, when Jerusalem filled with pilgrims. The disciples had waited, obeyed, gathered in one place with one heart. There's something holy about obedience before the gift.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A sound from heaven like rushing wind—the Spirit moves where He wills, sudden and unmistakable. The whole house shook with His presence, a physical sign of invisible power.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Tongues like fire, resting on each one—not harming but illuminating, like a lamp on each head. Each person receives the gift individually, even as they stand together.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Filled with the Holy Spirit and speaking new languages—the ability flowed from Him, not from their learning or effort. When the Lord gives voice, the mouth follows.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Devout Jews from every nation—pilgrims gathered for a holy feast, seekers in their own ways. The Lord draws from every corner of the known world.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Each heard in his own language—a reversal of Babel. Where once speech confused, now speech unites; where once people scattered, now they gather around the same Word.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Galileans! The accent was unmistakable, yet here they spoke with eloquence in foreign tongues. The disciples' humble origin made their words ring louder, not softer.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The question itself confesses wonder. We hear—each of us in the speech we were born into. The Spirit speaks the heart's native tongue, the language our mothers taught us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A roll call of nations from Parthia to Arabia—the scattered children of Israel and believers from every corner of the Empire, all present at the birth of the Church. The gospel has no borders.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Amazed and perplexed—the two marks of a true encounter with God. Our neat categories shatter, and we are left asking, 'What does this mean?' as if seeing for the first time.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Others mocking, speaking of new wine. There is always a crowd that reaches for easy mockery rather than the harder work of understanding. Their scorn becomes a mirror for us all.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Peter stood with the eleven. The denier had become the defender, the fearful man now raised his voice for the One he'd abandoned. Grace doesn't just forgive—it restores.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The third hour—nine in the morning, too early for drunkenness. Peter uses a simple fact to sweep aside the slander, speaking plainly to plain people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: This is what was spoken through the prophet. Peter shows them that Pentecost wasn't a surprise—the Lord had whispered it through His servants long before. History moves toward its fulfillment.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: 'In the last days'—when the Spirit is poured out, no one stays outside the circle. Sons and daughters, young and old receive visions and dreams alike. The hierarchy of the human order bows before His generosity.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: On my servants and handmaidens—even those in bonds will prophesy when the Spirit falls. Status means nothing. The Master sees and calls the hidden ones into His light.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Wonders in the sky, signs on the earth—creation itself will speak of judgment approaching. Yet within this solemn warning comes the invitation: anyone can still call on His name.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The sun turned to darkness, the moon to blood—cosmic signs point to the Lord's great day. Before that day arrives, hear the gentleness of His call: come now, while the door is open.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Whoever calls on His name will be saved. No exception clause, no small print—just the open door and the promise. A child's prayer, a thief's cry, a foreigner's tongue—all reach His ear.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jesus of Nazareth, a man approved by God through mighty works. Peter calls Him a man first—true and human—then tells what His works declare: divinity proven through mercies and wonders.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Delivered by God's determined counsel, yet taken by lawless hands. Peter doesn't soften the murder, nor does he hide God's purpose—both are named. Calvary sits at the center of all counsel.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God raised Him, freeing Him from death's agony. Three days in the grave couldn't hold Him. The constraint of death, unbreakable for all others, released its grip before the Holy One.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David's psalm—'I saw the Lord always before my face'—now reborn on Peter's lips as prophecy of the Messiah. The old king's words find their true meaning in the new King.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Heart glad, tongue rejoicing, flesh dwelling in hope—the whole person is caught up in trust. When the soul rests in the Lord, joy isn't forced; it flows like water finding its level.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: My soul not left in Hades, my flesh not seeing decay—the grave held Him for three days only. Even death served the purpose of the Holy One, and couldn't master Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Made known to me the ways of life—the resurrection paths are the Lord's own making. In His presence is fullness of joy; at His right hand are pleasures forevermore.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David's tomb is here among us. Peter appeals to plain fact that everyone can check—the patriarch died and was buried in Jerusalem, his bones still in the earth. The living Christ is different.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Being a prophet, David knew the oath—God had sworn His Messiah would come from his line and sit on his throne. David spoke what he knew only in part; now the meaning is plain.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Foreseeing the resurrection, David spoke truth he himself didn't live to see. His bones crumbled, but his words—alive in the Spirit—pointed to the One whose flesh saw no decay.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: This Jesus God raised up, to which we all are witnesses. Peter doesn't argue or philosophize—he points to what they all saw. Resurrection isn't theology; it's testimony lived by those who were there.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Exalted by God's right hand, He received the Spirit from the Father and poured it out. What they hear and see—tongues, power, presence—flows from the raised and glorified Jesus.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David didn't ascend to heaven—yet the psalmist wrote, 'The Lord said to my Lord.' Peter distinguishes between the earthly king and the heavenly King whose coming David foresaw.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Sit at My right hand until I make Your enemies a footstool—the promise extends until all opposition bends. The work isn't finished, but the outcome is certain, sworn by the Almighty.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Let all Israel know that Jesus—whom you crucified—is Lord and Christ. Peter doesn't hide the guilt, yet he doesn't wallow in it. He speaks the hard truth because the door to forgiveness is open.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Cut to the heart—pierced with the weight of what they'd done, yet not to despair. This is conviction, the Holy Spirit's work to wake us from our sleep and turn us homeward.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Repent and be baptized, every one of you. Peter offers the path plainly: turn around, be washed, receive the gift. No barrier but your own unwillingness stands between you and the Spirit.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The promise is to you and your children, and to all who are far off. Peter flings open the door—no nation, no generation is excluded. The Lord calls across every distance.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Save yourselves from this crooked generation. Peter speaks urgency without cruelty—don't be pulled along by the crowd's refusal. Step out. The way is open; the time is now.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Three thousand souls added that day. One sermon, one Spirit, one Lord—and the kingdom grew in an instant. When the gospel is preached in power, it bears immediate fruit.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They devoted themselves to teaching, fellowship, breaking bread, and prayer. The young church found its rhythm—not excitement alone, but steadfast habits that root us in community and truth.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Fear came on every soul—a holy reverence, not terror. When wonders are done through apostles, when the invisible becomes visible, how can we stand casual? Awe is the beginning of wisdom.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: All who believed were together, had all things in common. Not forced communism but voluntary generosity, the natural overflow of hearts united in the Lord. Love empties the pockets willingly.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They sold possessions and distributed to each as anyone had need. No one went hungry while another hoarded. The practical mercy of the poor-poor church—those with little gave from that little.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Daily in the temple and at home, breaking bread with gladness and singleness of heart. They met in both palace and cottage, formal and informal, together and in small groups—the church breathes with many lungs.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Praising God, having favor with all people; the Lord added daily to the assembly. Readers today hear an echo: when the church overflows with genuine praise and genuine love, even the watching world takes notice. The Spirit still draws those being saved.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
